description: Performance and SEO audit of acrylicon.no production site. Each story runs real measurements against production using Chrome MCP performance traces and curl-based HTML analysis. Goal: identify and document anything holding back PageSpeed scores, Core Web Vitals, or SEO visibility.

stories.title: Core Web Vitals — Norwegian homepage /no/
stories.description: Run a Chrome MCP performance trace on the Norwegian homepage with mobile emulation. This is the most important page — it's the main landing page for organic traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Set Chrome to mobile emulation: viewport 390x844, deviceScaleFactor 2, isMobile true, hasTouch true, CPU throttle 4x, network 'Fast 4G'
Navigate to https://acryli-28355.jana-osl.servebolt.cloud/no/
Run performance_start_trace with reload=true and autoStop=true
Save trace to scripts/ralph/tests/traces/no-homepage.json.gz
Document ALL performance insights returned — especially LCP, CLS, TBT/INP
For each insight with issues, run performance_analyze_insight to get details
Write findings to scripts/ralph/tests/results/01-cwv-no-homepage.md with: scores, problematic resources, specific recommendations
PASS if LCP < 2500ms AND CLS < 0.1. FAIL otherwise with exact values and causes
Also check list_console_messages for any JS errors

stories.title: Core Web Vitals — English homepage /
stories.description: Same performance trace on English homepage. Compare with Norwegian to catch locale-specific issues.
acceptance_criteria: Same mobile emulation as story 1
Navigate to https://acryli-28355.jana-osl.servebolt.cloud/
Run performance_start_trace with reload=true and autoStop=true
Save trace to scripts/ralph/tests/traces/en-homepage.json.gz
Document ALL insights, drill into any with issues
Write findings to scripts/ralph/tests/results/02-cwv-en-homepage.md
Compare with story 1 results — note any differences between EN/NO
PASS if LCP < 2500ms AND CLS < 0.1

stories.title: Core Web Vitals — Product page, reference page, office page
stories.description: Performance traces on the 3 other key page types. Each has different blocks and content — performance can vary.
acceptance_criteria: Same mobile emulation as story 1
Test these 3 pages with performance_start_trace (reload=true, autoStop=true):
1. /no/produkter/flake-system/ (product — heavy images, multiple blocks)
2. /no/referanser/rehabilitering-av-norges-idrettshogskole/ (reference — Gutenberg content)
3. /no/kontor/ (office page — simpler layout)
Save traces to scripts/ralph/tests/traces/ with descriptive names
Write combined findings to scripts/ralph/tests/results/03-cwv-inner-pages.md
For EACH page document: LCP value + LCP element, CLS value + shifting elements, largest resources, render-blocking resources
Drill into any performance insight that shows issues
PASS if ALL 3 pages have LCP < 2500ms AND CLS < 0.1

stories.title: Render-blocking resource audit
stories.description: Identify ALL render-blocking CSS and JS across the site. Every render-blocking resource delays First Contentful Paint and LCP.
acceptance_criteria: Curl https://acryli-28355.jana-osl.servebolt.cloud/no/ and extract ALL <link rel='stylesheet'> and <script> tags from <head>
Curl https://acryli-28355.jana-osl.servebolt.cloud/no/kontor/ (page WITHOUT slider) — same extraction
For each resource, document: URL, estimated size (curl -sI to get Content-Length), whether it's render-blocking (in <head> without async/defer), whether it's critical for above-the-fold
Flag any CSS/JS that loads on ALL pages but is only needed on some (waste)
Flag any third-party resources loaded synchronously
Check: is Swiper CSS/JS loading on /no/kontor/? (it should NOT be)
Check: are there any inline <style> blocks larger than 5KB? (should be external or critical-only)
Write audit to scripts/ralph/tests/results/04-render-blocking-audit.md
PASS if no unnecessary render-blocking resources found. FAIL with list of each wasteful resource and estimated impact

stories.title: Image optimization audit
stories.description: Audit all images on key pages for format, sizing, lazy loading, and fetchpriority. Images are typically the biggest PageSpeed bottleneck on content-heavy sites.
acceptance_criteria: Use Chrome MCP: navigate to /no/ with mobile emulation, take_snapshot to get all image elements

For EACH image on the page, check: format (WebP/AVIF preferred over JPEG/PNG), has width+height attributes (prevents CLS), loading='lazy' on below-fold images, fetchpriority='high' on LCP image only, srcset present for responsive serving, reasonable size (no 'full' size images on mobile)
Repeat for /no/referanser/ (archive with many thumbnails) and a single reference page
Use list_network_requests filtered to 'image' type to check actual transferred sizes
Flag any image > 200KB on mobile viewport
Flag any image served as PNG/JPEG when WebP exists
Flag any image without width/height (CLS risk)
Flag LCP image if it doesn't have fetchpriority='high'
Write audit to scripts/ralph/tests/results/05-image-audit.md with specific image URLs and recommendations
PASS if all above-fold images are optimized. FAIL with list of issues

stories.title: Third-party script and font loading audit
stories.description: Audit all third-party scripts (GTM, analytics, Byggfakta) and font loading strategy. Third-party scripts are the #1 cause of TBT/INP issues.
acceptance_criteria: Navigate to /no/ with Chrome MCP, list_network_requests to get ALL requests
Categorize each request: first-party vs third-party, resource type, transfer size, timing
Verify GTM is NOT loaded synchronously — should be delayed (setTimeout 3500ms or user interaction)
Check if any third-party script blocks main thread (visible in performance trace insights)
Audit font loading: are fonts preloaded? Do they use font-display: swap? How many font files total?
Check for preconnect hints to third-party domains (cdn.jsdelivr.net, fonts, analytics)
Check: is there a <meta name='theme-color'>?
Document total page weight breakdown: HTML, CSS, JS, images, fonts, third-party
Write audit to scripts/ralph/tests/results/06-third-party-font-audit.md
PASS if no synchronous third-party scripts and fonts are optimally loaded. FAIL with specifics

stories.title: SEO technical signals — crawlability and indexability
stories.description: Verify all technical SEO signals that affect how Google crawls and indexes the site. This is the foundation — if crawlability is broken, nothing else matters.
acceptance_criteria: Curl robots.txt on both / and /no/ — verify it exists, allows Googlebot, has sitemap reference
Curl sitemap (find URL from robots.txt) — verify it's valid XML, contains key pages, no broken URLs

For 6 key pages (EN home, NO home, product, reference single, reference archive, office): verify <meta name='robots'> allows indexing, <link rel='canonical'> is correct (self-referencing, absolute URL, HTTPS), <title> is unique per page and < 60 chars, <meta name='description'> is unique per page, 50-160 chars, contains relevant keywords
Check that 404 pages return actual HTTP 404 status (not soft 404): curl a non-existent URL
Check HTTP headers: X-Robots-Tag, correct Content-Type, proper cache headers
Verify HTTPS: no mixed content warnings, HTTP->HTTPS redirect works (curl -I http:// version)
Write audit to scripts/ralph/tests/results/07-seo-crawlability.md
PASS if all pages are indexable with correct canonicals. FAIL with specific issues

stories.title: SEO structured data — schema completeness and validity
stories.description: Extract and validate JSON-LD structured data on all page types. Correct schema = rich results in Google.
acceptance_criteria: For each page type, extract <script type='application/ld+json'> content and validate with jq:
Homepage (/no/): Organization (name, logo with valid URL, sameAs, contactPoint), WebSite (name, url, inLanguage='nb-NO', publisher ref), WebPage, BreadcrumbList
Product (/no/produkter/flake-system/): Product (name, brand, manufacturer ref, description, image with valid URL)
Reference single: Article (headline, datePublished in ISO8601, dateModified, publisher ref, image)
Office (single kontor): ProfessionalService (name, parentOrganization ref, telephone with +47, address, geo with lat/lng)
Archive (/no/referanser/): CollectionPage (url, name, isPartOf ref)
Verify ALL @id references actually resolve to existing nodes in the graph (no dangling refs)
Verify logo URL, og:image URL, and product image URL all return HTTP 200
Write audit to scripts/ralph/tests/results/08-schema-audit.md with full JSON-LD output per page type
PASS if all schemas are complete and valid. FAIL with specific missing/incorrect fields

stories.title: SEO hreflang and international targeting
stories.description: Verify hreflang implementation across EN/NO pairs. Broken hreflang = Google serves wrong language version to users.
acceptance_criteria: Test at least 4 page pairs: homepages, reference archive, a product page, the locations/contact page
For EACH page: extract all <link rel='alternate' hreflang='...'> tags
Verify reciprocity: if page A declares hreflang to page B, curl page B and verify it declares hreflang back to page A
Verify x-default always points to the English version
Verify language codes are consistent (en vs en-US, nb vs nb-NO — must be same format across all pages)
Verify all hreflang URLs are: absolute, HTTPS, canonical (not redirected URLs)
Curl each hreflang target URL and verify it returns HTTP 200 (not 404 or redirect)
Check html lang attribute matches the page language
Write audit to scripts/ralph/tests/results/09-hreflang-audit.md
PASS if all pairs are reciprocal and all URLs resolve. FAIL with broken pairs

stories.title: Mobile UX and PageSpeed visual verification
stories.description: Visual verification of mobile experience on key pages. Take screenshots, check for layout issues, verify tap targets and readability. This catches what automated metrics miss.
acceptance_criteria: Set Chrome to mobile: viewport 390x844, deviceScaleFactor 2, isMobile true, hasTouch true
For EACH of these 5 pages: /no/, /no/referanser/, /no/kontor/, a single reference, the locations page:
1. Navigate and wait for page load
2. Take full-page screenshot saved to scripts/ralph/tests/screenshots/{page-name}-mobile.png
3. Take snapshot (a11y tree) — check for proper heading hierarchy (h1 > h2 > h3, no skips)
4. Check list_console_messages for errors
5. Verify no horizontal overflow: evaluate_script to check document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= viewport width
6. On pages with phone numbers: verify they are <a href='tel:...'> links (check snapshot for 'link' role on phone numbers)
Verify navigation is accessible on mobile (hamburger menu or similar)
Take screenshot of /no/referanser/ and verify filter dropdowns are visible and usable
Write visual audit to scripts/ralph/tests/results/10-mobile-visual-audit.md with screenshot paths and findings
PASS if all pages render correctly on mobile with no errors. FAIL with specific issues and screenshot evidence
